name: proof-vscode
description: Runs the proof CLI (currently proof-java) and renders its verdict: inline coverage gutter, per-line test evidence, and mutation findings.

proof.jarPath.description: Path to proof-java.jar. Relative paths resolve against the workspace root. Leave empty to use the default search order (proof-java-cli/target/proof-java.jar, then .proof-java/proof-java.jar).

proof.javaExecutable.description: The Java executable used to run proof-java.jar.

proof.mavenExecutable.description: The Maven command used to generate a missing classpath list for Deep Scan. If left empty, "mvn.cmd" is used on Windows and "mvn" elsewhere. Set the full path if Maven isn't on PATH.

proof.coverageExclusions.description: Glob patterns in the style of sonar.coverage.exclusions (same syntax you'd paste into SonarQube). Passed to every analysis run as --coverage-exclusions - a single, hand-maintained list (D-05), never merged with the repo's own proof.config.json.

proof.reportPath.description: Path to the JaCoCo XML report (relative to the workspace root). "proof-java: Quick Scan" reads this file - if it's missing, you get a one-time prompt to fix the setting, not a repeat warning on every run.

proof.diffMode.description: What "new code" is measured against. uncommitted (default): everything not yet committed (staged + unstaged) - i.e. what's currently sitting in your working tree. base: changes since the commit/branch named in proof.baseRef (e.g. comparing a feature branch to main). no-vcs: git is never used, "new code" can't be computed - the whole repo is shown as one coverage figure. "proof-java: Deep Scan" does not run in this mode, because per-test evidence requires a diff.

proof.baseRef.description: The commit, branch, or tag to compare against when proof.diffMode is "base" (e.g. "main" or "origin/main"). Unused for other diffMode values. Setting this to HEAD itself, or to a ref that isn't an ancestor of HEAD, produces an empty diff - there's no real difference to compare.

proof.perTestClasspathPath.description: Path to the classpath list file (relative to the workspace root, one jar/output-dir per line) used by "proof-java: Deep Scan". Usually generated by "mvn dependency:build-classpath" - see the example run.ps1 in coverdict-playground.

proof.show.explorerBadges.description: Show a coverage-percentage badge next to every file and folder in the Explorer (e.g. "85" next to Calculator.java). Independent of proof.show.lineGutter: turning this off only removes the badges, editor line colors are unaffected.

proof.show.lineGutter.description: Draw a colored line to the left of each line in an open file, showing whether it's covered (green: covered, yellow: partial, red: uncovered - a different palette applies when proof.colorblindMode is on). Independent of proof.show.explorerBadges: turning this off only removes these lines, Explorer percentage badges are unaffected.

proof.colorblindMode.description: Use a palette that stays distinguishable under all three types of color blindness (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia) instead of red/green for line coverage (proof.show.lineGutter) - the Okabe-Ito palette: blue=covered, yellow=partial, vermillion=uncovered, purple="falsely green". Takes effect immediately in open editors, no window reload needed.

proof.show.oraclelessLines.description: Even when JaCoCo counts a line as covered, show it orange instead of green if NONE of the tests covering it has a real assertion (oracle) - i.e. every one of them produced a NO_RECOGNIZED_ORACLE/TAUTOLOGICAL_ORACLE/CATCH_ORACLE_WITHOUT_FAIL finding ("falsely green"). No line is ever marked this way unless per-test evidence (proof-java: Deep Scan or Which Test Covers Which Line For This Class) has actually been collected - no evidence, no accusation.

proof.badgeMetric.description: Which coverage mode drives Explorer badges and line coloring. sonar-compatible (default): matches SonarQube's own percentage within +/-0.1 - it also counts branch coverage, so it usually comes out lower than jacoco-line. jacoco-line: a line counts as covered if any instruction on it ran (the highest number you'll see). strict-line: a line only counts as covered if EVERY instruction on it ran (the strictest, usually the lowest number). The status bar and tooltips always show all three; this setting only picks one for the badge/line color.

proof.mutationTimeout.description: Time budget, in seconds, for one module in mutation testing (--mutation-timeout). If exceeded, the run stops and the result is partial - the partial result is still shown, never silently dropped. Single-class runs are usually seconds long; you may need to raise this for module-wide runs.

proof.perTestTimeout.description: Time budget, in seconds, for one module in Deep Scan (--per-test-timeout). If exceeded, the run stops (PER_TEST_COLLECTION_FAILED). The default is usually enough for a handful of classes changed in a diff; you may need to raise it for a run that targets many classes at once, such as "Deep Scan Whole Module Anyway".

proof.testCommandPhase.description: Which Maven phase "proof-java: Run Tests" runs. test (default): the shortest path, usually enough to produce the JaCoCo report. verify: needed if your modules require a packaged jar (e.g. a JPMS/OSGi test) - takes longer.

proof.jacocoPluginVersion.description: The org.jacoco:jacoco-maven-plugin version "proof-java: Run Tests" binds from the command line when the pom doesn't declare the JaCoCo plugin at all. Unused if the pom already declares its own JaCoCo version - the pom itself is never touched.

kind.description: The kind of task proof-java itself launches (e.g. runTests).

commands.title: proof-java: Which Test Covers Which Line For This Class
proof-java: Deep Scan Whole Module (no diff)
proof-java: Mutation Testing - Whole Module (no diff)

view/item/context.when: view == proof.qualityView || view == proof.coverageView || view == proof.lineTestsView || view == proof.mutationView

scripts.compile: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.package: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js --production
scripts.test: npm run test:unit && npm run test:integration
